modifier.description:
Value type modifier

Non empty constraint is specified by adding an exclamation mark in front of the ValueType:
```type
  where: !Location
```

The desire to preserve empty values (such that they can be differentiated from the lack of any value) is specified
by adding a question mark in front of the ValueType:
```type
  approved: ?boolean
```

The non optional function parameter constraint is specified by adding `!?` in front of the ValueType:
```type
  f: function(url: !?string serialized Url)
```

@see #isNonEmpty
@see #preservesEmpty
@see #isNonOptionalParam
@see FunctionParam#isNonOptional

keyType.description:
The value type for the keys that index the collection.
For array and set, the key is `int` and for stream is the key is not used.
For maps, the key can be any primitive type.

elementType.description: The value type for the elements of the collection.

title:
A set is a vector of a single value type, which cannot contain duplicates;
attempts to add duplicate values are ignored. Null values are not allowed.
Otherwise, the semantics of set are the same as {@link ArrayType array}.

Sets are declared in DSL using `set<E>` notation:

```
// zero or more primitive integers
counts: set<int>

// Cat objects or any type that mixes Cat
herd: set<Cat>
```

Instances can be created programatically using these convenience methods:
 - #of
 - #ofAny
 - #ofBinary
 - #ofBool
 - #ofByte
 - #ofDateTime
 - #ofDecimal
 - #ofDbl
 - #ofFloat
 - #ofInt
 - #ofInt16
 - #ofInt32
 - #ofJson
 - #ofNative
 - #ofStr

@see Set
name: SetType
